n:Acadian Asset Management: Acadian Asset Management is an investment management firm based in Boston, in the United States. The tie to a central bank is a shared person. Ajmal Ahmady worked as a sovereign analyst at Acadian from 2009 to 2012, between jobs at T. Rowe Price from 2008 to 2009 and Fortress Investment Group from 2012 to 2014, and later became Acting Governor of Da Afghanistan Bank, the Afghan central bank, from 3 June 2020 to 15 August 2021.
n:BNP Paribas El Djazaïr: BNP Paribas El Djazaïr is a bank in Algiers, Algeria. Its link to a central bank is one person's career. Mohamed Lamine Lebbou worked at BNP Paribas El Djazaïr from 2004 to 2006. He then headed the state-owned Banque nationale d'Algérie from 2021 to 2024 and BEA International Bank from May 2025, and was appointed Governor of the Banque d'Algérie, the Bank of Algeria, in February 2026.
n:Banco de Reservas: Banco de Reservas is a bank in Santo Domingo, in the Dominican Republic. One central bank is tied to it through a shared person. George Manuel Hazoury was an administrator of Banco de Reservas before becoming a member of the Junta Monetaria, the monetary board of the Banco Central de la República Dominicana. He sat on that board until he was replaced under decree 532-20 in 2020.
n:Banco di Caribe: Banco di Caribe is a bank in Willemstad, Curaçao. One central bank is tied to it through a shared person. José Jardim was Financial Economic Director and a member of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Curaçao and Sint Maarten from 2017 until 30 June 2025. He then became Chief Executive Officer of Banco di Caribe, effective 1 July 2025.
n:Bank of Bhutan: Bank of Bhutan is a bank in Thimphu, Bhutan. Damche Tenzin worked at Bank of Bhutan Limited as Chief Legal Advisor and Company Secretary, then as Chief Support Officer, from September 2008 to December 2014. He went on to be Chief General Counsel of the National Pension & Provident Fund, and from 1 June 2016 Chief General Counsel of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the country's central bank.
n:Branislav Gulev: Branislav Gulev is in Skopje, North Macedonia. He took part in the State Audit Office's audit of the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia's 2003 financial statements. The final report of 4 March 2005 found improper and unlawful use of funds: the bank had guaranteed a domestic bank with foreign-currency deposits, and in January 2004 foreign banks drew 20,759,515 US dollars from its guarantee deposit. It also found purchases of 30,210 thousand denars made without following the Public Procurement Law.
n:Fortress Investment Group: Fortress Investment Group is an investment firm based in New York, in the United States. The tie to a central bank is a shared person. Ajmal Ahmady worked in emerging market trading at Fortress from 2012 to 2014, after a fixed income job at T. Rowe Price from 2008 to 2009 and sovereign analysis at Acadian Asset Management from 2009 to 2012. He was Acting Governor of Da Afghanistan Bank, the Afghan central bank, from 3 June 2020 to 15 August 2021.
n:Government of Samoa: The Government of Samoa, in Apia, pressed ahead with changes to the Central Bank of Samoa's law widening the Finance Minister's role and moving some of the bank's rules into regulations. In a letter to the Attorney-General's office the bank said the changes could weaken its independence, increase political influence and create legal uncertainty. The International Monetary Fund wrote to Finance Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molio'o on 9 April 2026 with the same warning about the bank's autonomy; Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt rejected the warnings as outside interference.
n:Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao S: Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt is the Prime Minister of Samoa, in Apia. His government pressed ahead with changes to the Central Bank of Samoa's law that would widen the Finance Minister's role and move some of the bank's rules into regulations. The International Monetary Fund wrote to Finance Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molio'o on 9 April 2026 warning the reforms could weaken the bank's autonomy, and Schmidt rejected those warnings as outside interference. The central bank itself had told the Attorney-General's office the changes could weaken its independence.
n:Liberty Life Lesotho: Liberty Life Lesotho is a company based in Maseru, Lesotho. Its tie to a central bank is a shared person. Mrs M. Mohasoa was a member of its board and chairman of its audit and risk committee from 2017 to 2021, and later became a non-executive director of the Central Bank of Lesotho, which issues the country's money.
n:Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah is the President of Namibia, in Windhoek. In the question-and-answer session after her State of the Nation Address she said the reported losses at the Bank of Namibia, Namibia's central bank, together with missing Government Institutions Pension Fund money, were smelling of corruption and must be investigated. Job Amupanda, leader of Affirmative Repositioning, said the central bank had made a loss close to a billion dollars for unexplained reasons. These are remarks, not findings, and no investigation is reported as ordered.
n:Samoa Audit Office: The Samoa Audit Office is based in Apia, Samoa. Its 2014 performance audit of government debt servicing compared when repayments were due with the dates the Central Bank of Samoa actually made them, and found instances where repayments had been delayed. It also recorded that there was no formalised arrangement between the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank. Its recommendations went to the Ministry of Finance, including that the two bodies formalise their responsibilities. No wrongdoing by any person is alleged.
n:Spitamen Bank: Spitamen Bank is a bank in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Four officials of the National Bank of Tajikistan, the country's central bank, have moved to its boards. Navruz Samandarzoda, who headed the central bank's research and modelling department, joined in January 2018 and later became Chairman of its Management Board. Sanovbar Dzhabirova, deputy director of the central bank's accounting department, and Mahmud Hamralizoda, deputy head of its international relations department, joined the Supervisory Board in January 2023, and Dilbar Khuseynova, head of insurance control from 2017 to 2024, in October 2024.
n:Standard Bank Group: Standard Bank Group is a stock-exchange-listed private banking group in Johannesburg, South Africa. Mrs M. Mohasoa, a non-executive director of the Central Bank of Lesotho, was a member of the board and chairman of the audit and risk committee of the insurer Liberty Life Lesotho from 2017 to 2021. Ownership is documented: the South African Reserve Bank's list of designated entities names Liberty Life Lesotho Ltd within the Liberty Insurance Group, and Liberty Holdings' 2019 annual report states Standard Bank Group Limited holds 53.6% of Liberty's issued ordinary share capital.
n:State Audit Office of the Republic of: The State Audit Office of the Republic of Macedonia, based in Skopje, audited the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia's 2003 accounts from 12 October to 20 December 2004. Its final report of 4 March 2005 found improper and unlawful use of funds: the bank had guaranteed a domestic bank with foreign-currency deposits, and in January 2004 foreign banks drew 20,759,515 US dollars from its guarantee deposit. It also found 30,210 thousand denars of purchases, 35.61 percent of those audited, made without following the Public Procurement Law.
n:T. Rowe Price: T. Rowe Price is an investment management firm based in Baltimore, in the United States. Ajmal Ahmady was a fixed income analyst there from 2008 to 2009. He then worked as a sovereign analyst at Acadian Asset Management from 2009 to 2012 and in emerging market trading at Fortress Investment Group from 2012 to 2014, and was Acting Governor of Da Afghanistan Bank, the Afghan central bank, from 3 June 2020 to 15 August 2021.
n:United Group Holdings: United Group Holdings is a privately held group in Willemstad, Curaçao, headed by Curaçao businessman Gregory Elias. It has wholly owned the commercial bank Banco di Caribe since 2022. José Jardim, a board member of the Central Bank of Curaçao and Sint Maarten since 2017 responsible for financial and economic supervision and monetary policy, became chief executive of Banco di Caribe effective 1 July, ending an eight-year tenure at the central bank. The central bank announced his departure effective 30 June 2025 without naming his new employer.
